-- stackbuf/go.mod --
module example.com/optlevels/stackbuf

go 1.27

-- stackbuf/stackbuf.go --
package stackbuf

-- stackbuf/stackbuf_test.go --
package stackbuf

import (
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"testing"
)

// probe is a frame-local make of variable size. The compiler keeps it in
// the frame when n is at most the stack buffer of the build.
//
//go:noinline
func probe(n int) byte {
	b := make([]byte, n)
	b[0] = 1
	return b[n-1]
}

func allocs(n int) float64 {
	return testing.AllocsPerRun(10, func() { _ = probe(n) })
}

func TestCompiledStackBuffer(t *testing.T) {
	want, err := strconv.Atoi(os.Getenv("WANT_STACKBUF"))
	if err != nil || want < 2 {
		t.Fatalf("WANT_STACKBUF=%q: want a byte count of at least 2", os.Getenv("WANT_STACKBUF"))
	}
	for _, c := range []struct {
		n     int
		stack bool
	}{
		{want / 2, true},
		{want, true},
		{want + 1, false},
		{2*want + 1, false},
	} {
		if got := allocs(c.n); (got == 0) != c.stack {
			t.Errorf("make of %d bytes took %v allocations, want the stack buffer of %d bytes to decide: stack=%v", c.n, got, want, c.stack)
		}
	}
}

// appendProbe appends n bytes to a frame-local slice and reports the final
// capacity and whether every byte survived.
//
//go:noinline
func appendProbe(n int) (int, bool) {
	s := make([]byte, 0)
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		s = append(s, byte(i))
	}
	for i := range s {
		if s[i] != byte(i) {
			return cap(s), false
		}
	}
	return cap(s), true
}

// TestBufferBacksAppends proves the buffer is used, not only sized: appends
// inside it take no heap allocation, one byte past it does, capacity covers
// the whole buffer, and the bytes survive the move to the heap.
func TestBufferBacksAppends(t *testing.T) {
	want, err := strconv.Atoi(os.Getenv("WANT_STACKBUF"))
	if err != nil || want < 2 {
		t.Fatalf("WANT_STACKBUF=%q: want a byte count of at least 2", os.Getenv("WANT_STACKBUF"))
	}
	if a := testing.AllocsPerRun(10, func() { appendProbe(want) }); a != 0 {
		t.Errorf("appending %d bytes inside the buffer took %v allocations, want none", want, a)
	}
	if c, ok := appendProbe(want); !ok {
		t.Errorf("data lost after appending %d bytes inside the buffer", want)
	} else if c < want {
		t.Errorf("capacity after %d appends is %d, want at least the buffer size", want, c)
	}
	if a := testing.AllocsPerRun(10, func() { appendProbe(want + 1) }); a < 1 {
		t.Errorf("appending %d bytes, one past the buffer, took no heap allocation", want+1)
	}
	if _, ok := appendProbe(want + 1); !ok {
		t.Errorf("data lost across the move past %d bytes", want)
	}
}
